title: How to Train Your Will to Want to Teach Again, Despite Everything https://davestuartjr.com/how-to-train-your-will-to-want-to-teach-again-despite-everything-principles
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: In the opening post of a summer 2020 series on sustaining "the will to teach," Dave Stuart Jr. names the exhaustion and disillusionment many teachers felt after four months of pandemic disruption, then argues that the will to teach — like a muscle or a language — can be deliberately trained even though it can never be made perfect. He lays out four principles: the will is trainable but not perfectible; its training is influenced by the state of the mind and body; and meaningful transformation is achievable through consistent, evidence-informed practice rather than raw willpower alone. The piece ends with a single, deliberately small first practice — simply deciding, after a walk and some reflection, whether you actually want to rebuild your will to teach — setting up the more concrete practices that follow later in the series.
points: Stuart's central claim is that the will to teach is trainable but never fully "perfectible," a distinction he insists must be held simultaneously to avoid both despair and complacency.

He draws a direct analogy to physical and language training (squatting 300 pounds, learning conversational Japanese) to argue that time-bound, structured practice — not willpower alone — produces real capacity change.
The piece distinguishes between dumb, faddish approaches to building the will to teach and smart, evidence-rich ones, foreshadowing more concrete practices later in the series.
The first prescribed "practice" is deliberately minimal: a walk and a simple yes/no decision about whether to pursue the work, modeling the low-friction, sustainable approach the series champions.
quotes: I haven't quite fancied a career change, but I have known that weight. It is not something new to the COVID days, but the disruption of COVID has made it heavier.
Just as the body can be trained to walk or bench press, and the mind can be trained to speak French or do calculus, the heart can be trained to will a thing that it previously could not.
There will always be times when we don't want to teach, don't want to do what is right as a teacher, don't want to bring our full selves to the work.

This is one of the most exciting things about being a person: we come with the built-in ability to learn and grow (potential). But it's also one the most limiting things about being a person: we can't just will ourselves to learn and grow.
There are smart, evidence-rich ways to increase your squat capacity, and there are dumb, faddish, evidence-poor ways to do so.
Do you intend to improve your will to teach? Do you want to want to teach again? Do you wish the fires of passion were burning brighter in you? Do you miss the earnestness you once felt?
